source: NCERT Class X, India and the Contemporary World II, History Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation
points: The **French Revolution (1789)** first spread the idea of the **nation** — sovereignty resting with the **people**, not the king.
It created a sense of collective identity: **la patrie** (the fatherland) and **le citoyen** (the citizen); a national flag (tricolour), anthem, and uniform laws.
**Napoleon** spread revolutionary ideas across Europe (the **Civil Code / Napoleonic Code, 1804** — equality before law, abolished feudal privileges).

sections.heading: 2. Liberalism and the 1848 Revolutions
points: **Liberal nationalism** (early 19th c.): **liberalism** meant individual freedom, equality before law, and government by consent; for the middle class, also **freedom of markets**.
The **Vienna Congress (1815)** restored conservative monarchies after Napoleon's fall.
**Giuseppe Mazzini** founded **Young Italy** and **Young Europe** — a key nationalist visionary.
**1848 revolutions** demanded constitutions and nation-states (the 'springtime of peoples').

sections.heading: 3. Unification of Germany and Italy
points: **Germany:** unified (1866–1871) by **Otto von Bismarck** (Prussia) through **'blood and iron'** (wars); **Kaiser Wilhelm I** proclaimed German Emperor (1871).
**Italy:** **Cavour** (PM of Sardinia-Piedmont) led diplomacy; **Giuseppe Garibaldi** and his 'Red Shirts' liberated the south; **Victor Emmanuel II** became King of a united Italy (1861).
**Britain** became a nation-state gradually (Act of Union 1707 — England + Scotland).

sections.heading: 4. Nationalism and Symbols
points: Nations were personified as female figures: **Marianne** (France) and **Germania** (Germany).
By the late 19th c., nationalism turned **narrow and aggressive (imperialist)**.
The **Balkans** became a region of intense nationalist rivalry (the 'powder keg of Europe') → helped trigger **World War I (1914)**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: French Revolution (1789) spread the idea of the nation; Napoleonic Code (1804) = equality before law.
Congress of Vienna 1815 (conservative restoration); Mazzini = Young Italy/Young Europe.
Germany unified by Bismarck ('blood and iron'); Kaiser Wilhelm I, 1871.
Italy: Cavour (diplomacy), Garibaldi (Red Shirts), Victor Emmanuel II (1861).
Symbols: Marianne (France), Germania (Germany); Balkans = 'powder keg of Europe'.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Germany = Bismarck** ('blood and iron'); **Italy = Cavour + Garibaldi + Mazzini**.
**Marianne = France; Germania = Germany** (national personifications).
The **Congress of Vienna (1815)** was **conservative** (restored monarchies).
The **Balkans** ('powder keg') fuelled aggressive nationalism → WWI.
